perspective:
Ethan’s available information is:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a Black man and plumber. Gary Guo is his close, long-time friend from middle school, now an Asian doctor. They rely on each other for support.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned and invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- Gary initially told Ethan he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital. Ethan later was at the retreat with Gary.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more going on than work obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he did not want to burden Ethan.
- After that, Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy, suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities, and Gary agreed, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. Ethan heard Gary say things were better, that Ethan’s help made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie. Ethan felt hopeful and proud, encouraged Gary, and said he was there whenever Gary needed to talk.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing better on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always a call away but knew Gary could handle it. Gary thanked him, said he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
